The survey produced the following results as shown in Fig. 5. | • 78 participants had knowledge about a drone and swarm of drones whereas 100 of them understood what a drone is but did not know about the swarm of drones. However, 9 of the participants had never even heard about drone technology. • Only 43 participants had used drones as a hobby, work, building inspection, counting of cows, research, First-person view (FPV), photography, filming, and/or leisure activities. • 115 participants mentioned having security concerns whereas 6 of them had privacy concerns, and 8 had security as well as privacy concerns. Only 1 participant added that any type of concerns was dependent on the functional capabilities of drones. On the other hand, 57 participants had no concerns at all in case of the use of a swarm of drones for surveillance. • 113 participants were of the view that the use of drones was better for surveillance, 37 did not see any difference in either way, and 33 of the participants preferred to use traditional surveillance ways. 4 answers were discarded due to lack of information given. • Table 4 shows the participants categorized as per the field in which they used or intended to use the drone technology.
